stories.headline: Very Severe Cyclone Arnab Is Due to Hit Andhra Pradesh in the Early Hours of 28 October
stories.what_happened: Cyclone Arnab strengthened into a very severe cyclonic storm over the Bay of Bengal. The India Meteorological Department's 5:30 pm bulletin on 27 October forecast landfall between 2 am and 4 am on 28 October near Visakhapatnam. More than 114,000 people have been moved from vulnerable coastal districts of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.
stories.why_it_matters: Wind at this speed can badly damage buildings, so moving people to shelters before landfall protects lives.
stories.geography: Bay of Bengal; east coast of India; Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh; southern Odisha

key_facts.fact: At Andhra Pradesh landfall the IMD expects winds of 125 to 135 kmph, gusting up to 150 kmph.
The IMD's 5:30 pm bulletin forecast an early landfall between 2 am and 4 am on 28 October, near Visakhapatnam.
More than 114,000 residents were relocated from vulnerable coastal districts: more than 84,000 in Andhra Pradesh and more than 30,000 in Odisha.
About 4,000 cyclone shelters are set up across the two states, including 2,131 in Andhra's coastal districts.
Andhra Pradesh deployed 1,087 medical teams, 1,274 ambulances and 8,281 emergency beds, and moved 1,351 pregnant women to hospitals.
At least 21 flights were cancelled at Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam on Tuesday, and at least 50 trains were cancelled.
Odisha closed schools in 16 of its 30 districts.
The southern Odisha coast may see winds of 60 to 80 kmph.
Andhra Pradesh's Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu said there is no need for people to panic but they have to take precautions.
More than 12 million people live along the projected path of the storm.
The storm formed over the Bay of Bengal, a major breeding ground for tropical cyclones that frequently affects India's eastern coast.
At the time of Al Jazeera's report the storm was 260 km southeast of Visakhapatnam and forecast to turn northwest.
More than 30,000 fishing boats were secured along the Andhra Pradesh coast, and over 2,000 cyclone shelters were set up across 20 districts.
Odisha officials planned to evacuate about 48,000 people from areas likely to be affected.
Heavy rain and gusty winds had already started lashing parts of the Andhra Pradesh coast on Tuesday, and officials cancelled some train services.

stories.headline: Oil Stays Above $114 as Attacks on Saudi Arabia Continue and Gulf Talks Begin
stories.what_happened: Brent crude settled at $115.81 a barrel on Monday 26 October and was near $114.68 early on Tuesday. Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia have continued: the Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed three drones aimed at Riyadh and southern regions on Monday. Also on Monday, officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan met Iran's leadership in Tehran.
stories.why_it_matters: Saudi Arabia is a giant oil exporter, so attacks and talks in the Gulf move fuel prices for families far away.
stories.geography: Saudi Arabia (Riyadh, Yanbu, Shaybah); Yemen; Iran (Tehran); Strait of Hormuz and the Gulf

key_facts.fact: Monday's settlements were Brent $115.81 a barrel (briefly above $117 during the day) and WTI $101.76.
On Tuesday 27 October in early Asian trade Brent was $114.68 and WTI $100.83.
On Monday senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan met Iran's leadership in Tehran; Iranian state media said the states agreed to keep talking.
CNBC reported that Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian.
Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia have continued; the Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed three drones aimed at Riyadh and southern regions on Monday.

On 19 October the Houthis said they attacked Saudi energy, airport and military targets including an Aramco facility in Yanbu, the Shaybah oilfield and Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport; Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm, and Reuters could not verify the claims.

Increased threats to commercial shipping cut crude flows through the Hormuz region to about 8.5 million barrels a day in the week to 19 October, down from more than 20 million the week before, according to Kpler.
Gulf crude exports fell for a fourth straight week, and flows through the Strait of Hormuz were about 60% of their normal level.
The Houthis said they hit pumping stations on Saudi Arabia's East-West crude pipeline and Riyadh airport over the weekend, with no immediate Saudi confirmation.
Brent settled at $116.72 on Friday 23 October, its highest close since April, capping a 6% weekly gain.
On Monday Brent settled 91 cents lower at $115.81 and WTI fell $1.51 to $101.76.
Global distillate inventories were nearly 5% below their five-year average.

stories.headline: Ukraine, Russia and the US Agree to Hold Three-Way Talks Next Month
stories.what_happened: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on 26 October that Ukraine, Russia and the US have agreed to hold three-way talks next month. He renewed his call for a meeting with Putin on territorial issues. Russia says the talks will not pause the fighting.
stories.why_it_matters: Talks are how wars can end, but both sides still disagree about land.

key_facts.fact: Zelenskyy said Ukraine, Russia and the US have agreed to hold trilateral talks next month; the report gives no exact date or venue.
Zelenskyy renewed his call for a meeting with Putin to discuss territorial issues.
Putin said the aim is lasting security through final peace agreements, not a short-lived ceasefire.
Russia has said it has no intention of halting hostilities during the peace talks.
Putin aide Yuri Ushakov said Russia had agreed in principle to meet on 10 November; Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said the meeting would be held in Abu Dhabi.
Zelenskyy said Russia supports a trilateral meeting at the level of the negotiating teams.
Zelenskyy said any peace agreement would need strong security guarantees for Ukraine and funding for 10 years to maintain the Ukrainian army.
The last US-mediated peace talks took place in February, before the United States and Israel launched a war against Iran.
US envoy Steve Witkoff met Zelenskyy in Oslo on 20 October and Putin in St Petersburg the next day.
Russia demands that Ukraine pull out of the territory it still controls in the eastern Donetsk region; Ukraine rejects this as tantamount to capitulation.
Russia and Ukraine both said they were ready to resume trilateral talks with Washington after Witkoff met both leaders.
A localised ceasefire around the occupied city of Oleshky took effect early on Tuesday 27 October to allow humanitarian aid; Russia, Ukraine and the US have not said who would monitor it.

Finland's President Alexander Stubb and Norway's leader held a rare direct call with Putin on Tuesday 27 October; Stubb's office said it was initiated from Helsinki to discuss diplomatic efforts to end the war.
The Kremlin's readout played down the call, said lasting peace depends on Russia's interests being fully taken into account, and blamed EU and NATO policies for prolonging the fighting.
Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said she was very sceptical about reaching out to Putin and urged Europe to act together.
On 20 October Zelenskyy, US envoy Steve Witkoff and European leaders met in Oslo to discuss ending the war.
The Kremlin dismissed new ideas brought by Witkoff that were developed with European countries and Ukraine; Ushakov said there wasn't really much substance in them.
Ushakov said Russia was in principle ready to resume trilateral talks in mid-November, after the US midterm elections.

stories.headline: Israel Votes, and Exit Polls Show No Clear Winner
stories.what_happened: Israelis voted in a national election on 27 October. Exit polls suggest neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor his main rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, won outright. Final results had not been published.
stories.why_it_matters: No party has enough seats alone, so the next government has to be built from several parties.

key_facts.fact: A majority in Israel's Knesset needs 61 of the 120 seats.
CNN reported that Netanyahu and his main rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, appear short of outright victory, according to exit polls.
Channel 12's exit poll projected the prime minister's bloc falling from 68 seats in the previous Knesset to 50 seats.
Turnout was reportedly the highest since at least 1999.
Exit polls are not final counts; official results come from the Central Elections Committee.
Channel 12's exit poll put Netanyahu's bloc on track for 50 seats and Gadi Eisenkot's bloc for 52.
Channel 14, which is strongly pro-Netanyahu, showed the prime minister's coalition at 60 seats and Eisenkot's at 43.
Turnout was 77.7%, the highest since 1999, according to Israel's Central Elections Committee; some 5.7 million voters cast ballots.
Likely weeks of coalition negotiations follow; President Isaac Herzog will ask a candidate to try to form a government.
Eisenkot has all but ruled out forming a government with Arab parties, complicating his path to a majority.
Channel 13 and Channel 11 (Kan) exit polls had Netanyahu's bloc and the opposition bloc tied at 51 seats each.
Likud was projected at close to 27 seats, appearing to be the largest party; Eisenkot's Yashar party was projected at roughly 21 to 22 seats.
Arab parties were projected at a combined 17 to 18 seats, outside both blocs.

stories.headline: More Than 30 Million Americans Have Voted Early a Week Before the Midterms
stories.what_happened: With a week to go before the 3 November midterm elections, more than 30 million Americans have already voted, according to election trackers. Early voting in Louisiana ends on Tuesday, and more than 363,000 people have voted there.
stories.why_it_matters: Early voting lets people vote before election day, and big numbers show many are taking part.

key_facts.fact: More than 30 million Americans have already voted with a week to go before the 3 November midterm elections.
Early voting in Louisiana ends on Tuesday 27 October; more than 363,000 people have already cast ballots there.

AP analysis of data through 20 October found early voting up 74% in Texas versus the same point in 2022, more than doubled in Kansas, and up more than 30% in Maine, North Carolina and Ohio; Republicans were a smaller share of early voters than four years earlier in most of these states.
Early voting in Texas runs 19 to 30 October; more than 4 million Texans had voted a week in; in Harris County more than 104,000 voted in person on day one, a first-day midterm record.
Texas Senate candidates are Ken Paxton (R), James Talarico (D) and Ted Brown (L); University of Houston's Nancy Sims said it is a little hard to extrapolate from turnout.
One week before Election Day, more than 31 million people had voted early, according to data from 47 states and the District of Columbia.
About 14.3 million voters had cast ballots by 21 October, according to the University of Florida's Election Lab.

stories.headline: The Fed Meets This Week as Families Watch Loan Costs
stories.what_happened: The US Federal Reserve's two-day meeting began on Tuesday 27 October, with its decision due on Wednesday 28 October at 2 pm US Eastern time. Traders put about an 11% chance on a rate hike this week, according to Reuters.
stories.why_it_matters: The Fed's rate influences what it costs to borrow money for homes, cars and credit cards.

key_facts.fact: The two-day FOMC meeting began Tuesday 27 October; the decision is due Wednesday 28 October at 2 pm EDT.
Traders priced about an 11% chance of a rate hike this week and about 82% for December, according to Reuters.
Fed funds futures point to about a 10% chance of a hike this week and a better than 80% probability of an increase in December.
Most credit cards carry variable rates that move closely with the Fed's benchmark; the average rate on a new credit card offer is 23.96%, according to LendingTree.
The 10-year Treasury yield has been near 5%, keeping the average 30-year fixed mortgage rate close to 7.4%, according to Mortgage News Daily.
Because the Fed has kept rates high, savers earn relatively attractive yields on high-yield savings accounts.
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh has repeatedly rejected telling markets what he plans to do before the committee meets.
A CNBC survey of 30 economists and strategists found 93% expect a pause this week and 76% a hike in December.
Traders on Kalshi priced a 93% chance the Fed holds steady this week; the status quo is a target range of 3.75% to 4.00%.

stories.headline: The Rupee Weakens Past 95 to the Dollar as Oil Stays Near $115
stories.what_happened: The rupee slipped to about 95.22 per US dollar in early trade on Tuesday 27 October, weighed down by high oil prices and a stronger dollar ahead of the US Fed decision. A provisional close of 95.12 was reported.
stories.why_it_matters: India buys much of its oil from abroad, so a weaker rupee makes imports such as fuel cost more.

key_facts.fact: The rupee fell 7 paise to 95.22 against the US dollar in early trade on 27 October.
Another report gives a provisional close of 95.12, helped by RBI support, with crude near $116.
On 7 October the RBI raised its repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5% and the Sensex closed at 72,638.70.
The rupee settled 22 paise lower at 95.15 on Monday, its third straight day of decline, losing 77 paise over three sessions.
The dollar index rose 0.06% to 101.86; foreign institutional investors sold net equities worth Rs 1,462.49 crore on Monday.
Forex traders said the rupee showed some recovery on likely RBI intervention but failed to withstand foreign fund outflows.
Analysts attributed higher crude to Houthi-led attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure; Sensex settled at 73,598.67 and Nifty at 22,749.75 on Monday.
Anuj Choudhary of Mirae Asset Sharekhan expects the rupee to trade with a negative bias and USD-INR between Rs 94.85 and Rs 95.50.
Business Recorder reported the rupee ended Tuesday 27 October at 95.1150 per dollar, with higher oil prices and equity outflows leaving it reliant on Reserve Bank of India support.
India depends on imports to meet nearly 90% of its crude oil requirements.
On 22 October the rupee weakened to 94.83 per dollar, ending eight sessions of gains, as crude prices and dollar buying offset inflows.
The RBI said it would meet the entire daily dollar needs of Indian Oil Corporation, HPCL and BPCL through a special window from 12 October.

stories.headline: Rubin Observatory Finds Its First Dwarf Planet Candidate
stories.what_happened: Astronomers using the Vera C. Rubin Observatory found a possible dwarf planet beyond Neptune, provisionally named 2026 ED138. It is about 1,000 km across and sits about 46 astronomical units from the Sun. More observations are needed before it can be confirmed.
stories.why_it_matters: It shows that our solar system still has large worlds to discover in the far, dim edge.
stories.geography: outer solar system beyond Neptune; observatory sees the Southern Hemisphere sky

key_facts.fact: The dwarf planet candidate is provisionally named 2026 ED138 and is estimated at 600 to 1,500 km across; Mario Juric says it is roughly 1,000 km across.
It is about 46 astronomical units from the Sun; Pluto averages 40 au.
On 13 October Matthew Holman ran Rubin data through a search code he wrote with Kevin Napier; the code matches billions of moving-object detections to find those belonging to the same object.
Mario Juric of the University of Washington, who leads Rubin's solar system team, confirmed it with 20 more observations going back to March 2026.
The team traced more than ten years of its orbit using archival images dating to 2016.
If confirmed it would join the five dwarf planets recognised by the International Astronomical Union: Pluto, Ceres, Eris, Haumea and Makemake.
Rubin's Legacy Survey of Space and Time began in June 2026; in April the team announced over 11,000 new asteroids, including roughly 380 new trans-Neptunian objects.
2026 ED138 was found in Rubin observations spanning 4 March to 11 July 2026.
Matthew Holman, who found it, works at the Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian.
The International Astronomical Union's Minor Planet Center announced the discovery in an electronic circular.
Mario Juric and Matthew Holman presented the result at the 58th meeting of the Division for Planetary Sciences in Spokane.
Further observations are needed to tell whether it has enough mass to pull itself into a round shape, a key requirement for a dwarf planet.
It stayed hidden for years because it sits in a star-crowded part of the sky.
If confirmed, ED138 would be among the largest dwarf planets ever discovered in this region of the Solar System.
Rubin observed ED138 30 times on 20 nights between 4 March and 11 July 2026.
Archival images from the Dark Energy Camera, found by the Asteroid Institute's ADAM Precovery service, gave data going back to 2016.
The 600 to 1,500 km size estimate is based on ED138's distance, brightness and estimated surface reflectivity (albedo).
Initial analysis indicates it may be among the largest and brightest bodies discovered in this region of the Solar System.

stories.headline: Chancellor John Healey Delivers His First Budget on 28 October
stories.what_happened: Chancellor John Healey, 101 days into the job, is due to present his first Budget to the House of Commons on 28 October. It is expected to be a 'steady-as-she-goes' Budget, with support on energy bills for poorer households and a freeze on fuel duty. Higher government borrowing costs linked to the Iran war have shrunk the room he has to spend.
stories.why_it_matters: A Budget decides taxes and spending, which touch household bills across the country.
stories.geography: United Kingdom; House of Commons, London

key_facts.fact: John Healey has been Chancellor for 101 days and is set to present his fiscal plans to the House of Commons.
The Budget is expected to be 'steady-as-she-goes', meant to give 'breathing space' to hard-pressed households.
Expected measures: energy bills support for poorer households, a freeze on fuel duty, action to help first-time buyers and tax relief for smaller businesses.
Healey plans a new raid on banks and a crackdown on online retailers such as Amazon, eBay and Temu.

The Office for Budget Responsibility forecast a buffer of about 24 billion pounds in March; the Resolution Foundation estimates it has roughly halved to 12 billion pounds because of higher borrowing costs linked to the Iran war.
The personal allowance has been frozen at 12,570 pounds since 2022 and no major income tax changes are expected.
A new tax allowance is planned for low-income pensioners who would otherwise be pulled into the tax system for the first time.
Healey said the Budget will move money and power out of Westminster and into every postcode around Britain, and will meet the fiscal rules.
The OBR will publish its economic and fiscal forecast on the same day as the Budget.
UK inflation rose to 3.5% in September 2026 from 3.1% in August, driven mainly by fuel; motor fuels rose 30% in the year to September.
Average petrol reached 169.5p a litre, the highest in around four years, and diesel hit 192.5p, its highest since July 2022.

stories.headline: UK Prices Rise 3.5% in a Year as Fuel Costs Climb, on the Eve of the Budget
stories.what_happened: UK inflation rose to 3.5% in September from 3.1% in August, driven mainly by fuel. Average petrol reached 169.5p a litre, the highest in around four years, and diesel hit 192.5p.
stories.why_it_matters: Higher fuel prices make trips and deliveries cost more, which feeds into shop prices.

key_facts.fact: UK CPI inflation rose to 3.5% in September 2026, up from 3.1% in August, driven mainly by fuel.
Motor fuels rose 30% in the year to September, up from 23% in August.
Average petrol reached 169.5p per litre, the highest in around four years; diesel hit 192.5p, its highest since July 2022.
Reports attribute the fuel rise to the Iran war, which has squeezed global oil and gas supplies.
Some economists think the rise could prompt the Bank of England to raise interest rates next month.
The ONS said core inflation, which leaves out energy, food, alcohol and tobacco, rose from 2.6% to 2.8%, and services inflation rose from 3.4% to 3.7%.
The next Bank of England interest-rate decision is on 5 November, and the next ONS inflation figures are due on 18 November 2026.
Chancellor John Healey blamed the price rises on conflicts in the Middle East and Europe.

stories.headline: Cost-of-Living Anger Spreads Across Europe as Fuel Prices Climb
stories.what_happened: Protests over living costs and public services have spread across Europe. In France, weekend unrest led to 2,400 arrests; in Milan police clashed with protesters; in Portugal thousands marched against housing costs. The European Commission estimates the Iran conflict has cost Europe about 100 billion euros.
stories.why_it_matters: When fuel and energy cost more, family budgets tighten, and that can change politics.

key_facts.fact: The European Commission estimates the Iran conflict has cost Europe roughly 100 billion euros through disrupted trade and energy markets.
Gas prices have jumped about 140% and diesel prices have doubled.
Weekend unrest in France led to 2,400 arrests; President Macron said protesters' demands were legitimate while condemning violence and looting.
French energy prices rose 21.3% year on year in September, according to INSEE.
In Milan police clashed on Sunday with protesters over poor public services and rising living costs; thousands protested in Portugal on Saturday against housing costs.

stories.headline: Ukraine, Russia and the US Agree to Hold Three-Way Talks Next Month
stories.what_happened: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on 26 October that Ukraine, Russia and the US have agreed to hold three-way talks next month. He renewed his call for a meeting with Putin on territorial issues. Russia says the talks will not pause the fighting.
stories.why_it_matters: Talks are how wars can end, but both sides still disagree about land.

key_facts.fact: Zelenskyy said Ukraine, Russia and the US have agreed to hold trilateral talks next month; the report gives no exact date or venue.
Zelenskyy renewed his call for a meeting with Putin to discuss territorial issues.
Putin said the aim is lasting security through final peace agreements, not a short-lived ceasefire.
Russia has said it has no intention of halting hostilities during the peace talks.
Putin aide Yuri Ushakov said Russia had agreed in principle to meet on 10 November; Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said the meeting would be held in Abu Dhabi.
Zelenskyy said Russia supports a trilateral meeting at the level of the negotiating teams.
Zelenskyy said any peace agreement would need strong security guarantees for Ukraine and funding for 10 years to maintain the Ukrainian army.
The last US-mediated peace talks took place in February, before the United States and Israel launched a war against Iran.
US envoy Steve Witkoff met Zelenskyy in Oslo on 20 October and Putin in St Petersburg the next day.
Russia demands that Ukraine pull out of the territory it still controls in the eastern Donetsk region; Ukraine rejects this as tantamount to capitulation.
Russia and Ukraine both said they were ready to resume trilateral talks with Washington after Witkoff met both leaders.
A localised ceasefire around the occupied city of Oleshky took effect early on Tuesday 27 October to allow humanitarian aid; Russia, Ukraine and the US have not said who would monitor it.

Finland's President Alexander Stubb and Norway's leader held a rare direct call with Putin on Tuesday 27 October; Stubb's office said it was initiated from Helsinki to discuss diplomatic efforts to end the war.
The Kremlin's readout played down the call, said lasting peace depends on Russia's interests being fully taken into account, and blamed EU and NATO policies for prolonging the fighting.
Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said she was very sceptical about reaching out to Putin and urged Europe to act together.
On 20 October Zelenskyy, US envoy Steve Witkoff and European leaders met in Oslo to discuss ending the war.
The Kremlin dismissed new ideas brought by Witkoff that were developed with European countries and Ukraine; Ushakov said there wasn't really much substance in them.
Ushakov said Russia was in principle ready to resume trilateral talks in mid-November, after the US midterm elections.

stories.headline: Israel Votes, and Exit Polls Show No Clear Winner
stories.what_happened: Israelis voted in a national election on 27 October. Exit polls suggest neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor his main rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, won outright. Final results had not been published.
stories.why_it_matters: No party has enough seats alone, so the next government has to be built from several parties.

key_facts.fact: A majority in Israel's Knesset needs 61 of the 120 seats.
CNN reported that Netanyahu and his main rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, appear short of outright victory, according to exit polls.
Channel 12's exit poll projected the prime minister's bloc falling from 68 seats in the previous Knesset to 50 seats.
Turnout was reportedly the highest since at least 1999.
Exit polls are not final counts; official results come from the Central Elections Committee.
Channel 12's exit poll put Netanyahu's bloc on track for 50 seats and Gadi Eisenkot's bloc for 52.
Channel 14, which is strongly pro-Netanyahu, showed the prime minister's coalition at 60 seats and Eisenkot's at 43.
Turnout was 77.7%, the highest since 1999, according to Israel's Central Elections Committee; some 5.7 million voters cast ballots.
Likely weeks of coalition negotiations follow; President Isaac Herzog will ask a candidate to try to form a government.
Eisenkot has all but ruled out forming a government with Arab parties, complicating his path to a majority.
Channel 13 and Channel 11 (Kan) exit polls had Netanyahu's bloc and the opposition bloc tied at 51 seats each.
Likud was projected at close to 27 seats, appearing to be the largest party; Eisenkot's Yashar party was projected at roughly 21 to 22 seats.
Arab parties were projected at a combined 17 to 18 seats, outside both blocs.
